reason: The text depicts Hebrew leaders (Moses, Aaron, the priests, and elders) functioning as intermediaries following God's instructions. They are implementing protective boundaries and sanctification procedures on behalf of the divine—warning the people not to ascend Mount Sinai to prevent their destruction (מות יומת—'death shall surely come'). Moses even expresses concern about the people's welfare to God. The leaders' actions are regulatory and protective in nature, mandated by divine command for the people's safety and ritual purity, not antagonistic.
